summary: Upload orchestrator warmup causing sustained 429s for background backfill; guidance requested for rate plan / burst isolation
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightCart AI is running a staged background backfill of historical user vectors via our dedicated pool. During the staged rollout of the upload orchestrator (coordinated workers, exponential backoff and staggered start), they observed multiple tenants receiving sustained 429s for 20–30 minutes despite traffic being below their nominal token quota.

Impact:
- Several of BrightCart's backfill jobs stalled mid-run repeatedly, increasing total run time and cost.
- Customer reports unfair token exhaustion behavior: short-lived spikes early in a batch window that consume burst credit for subsequent workers.

Environment:
- Dedicated deployment (customer_dedicated_42) on prod:us-east-1
- Orchestrator version: v1.18.3
- Rate-limiter config: default tenant window = 60s, burst pool enabled, smoothing flag = on

Steps to reproduce (customer-supplied):
1) Start 120 worker instances with staggered start (10s jitter) to upload batches of 2048 tokens each.
2) Orchestrator performs exponential backoff on entry (3 retries, 200ms->1s->3s) and then continuous uploads.
3) Within first 10 minutes, monitoring shows tenant token window depletion and 429s returned from /v1/embeddings endpoints.

Observed behavior:
- 429s appear in waves with early spike followed by 20–30 minute soft-throttle.
- Token bucket shows burst credits consumed quickly by orchestrator preflight probes and health-checks from workers.

Expected behavior:
- Staged backfill should use burst credits conservatively to avoid long soft-throttle periods; workers should queue or gracefully backoff without exhausting tenant burst pool.

Logs/Diagnostics attached by customer:
- Upload coordinator traces (trace IDs: trace-20260311-1102-BC1, trace-20260311-1118-BC2)
- Tenant token-bucket metrics (timeseries csv)
- Orchestrator start logs and worker health-check logs

Customer request:
- Guidance on recommended rate plan and configuration for large, staged backfills on dedicated pools (separate burst pool? lower preflight frequency? request-based smoothing parameters?)
- Suggestions on orchestrator-side changes (start jitter, backoff curve, preflight suppression) to avoid early burst credit depletion.
comments: 2026-03-11 12:04 - Aisha Patel: Opened with initial customer artifacts and metrics. Asked customer for their current burst pool allocation and whether they run simultaneous interactive traffic.
2026-03-11 14:30 - Diego Morales: Acknowledged. Pulled tenant token-bucket history; saw matching sawtooth pattern that aligns with orchestrator starts. Added label 'investigating'.

2026-03-12 09:12 - SRE Team (Marin Chen): Initial hypothesis: preflight probes + concurrent worker warmup are double-counted against tenant burst. Requested kube readiness probe config and any background health pings.
2026-03-12 11:45 - Customer (BrightCartAI Onboarding): Confirmed readiness probe frequency is 5s and workers ping an internal status endpoint once per start. They can change to 30s if recommended.

2026-03-13 08:02 - Diego Morales: Ran a controlled simulation in staging with 50 workers and adjusted preflight to 30s; burst credit consumption dropped ~70% in first 5 minutes. Preparing recommended config bundle.
2026-03-13 15:21 - Aisha Patel: Shared draft recommendations with BrightCart and asked them to schedule a joint test window.
investigation_notes: Hypotheses: (1) Readiness/health checks from workers are counted as requests against tenant window and are front-loading burst consumption; (2) Orchestrator exponential backoff parameters cause synchronized retries that exceed burst-smoothing expectations; (3) Default burst pool size not large enough for short-lived fanout during backfill. Evidence: token-bucket timeseries, orchestrator logs show clustered preflight requests within first 2 minutes. Staging simulation (Diego) reproduced behavior; changing readiness probe frequency and adding jitter reduced early consumption. Also flagged router edge for possible double-counting of preflight headers (follow-up with edge team).
next_steps: 1) Provide BrightCart with a recommended config: increase tenant burst pool by 30% for backfill window OR enable temporary per-route burst allocation; set readiness probe to 30s during backfill; add 500ms base jitter and increase first backoff slot to 500ms. 2) Coordinate with Edge team to confirm preflight probes are not double-accounted. 3) Schedule joint test and monitor token-bucket in real time. 4) Document pattern in runbook and propose a new 'backfill' rate-plan template.
resolution: In Progress — recommended config bundle prepared and awaiting customer joint-test scheduling. Follow-up tasks: edge accounting verification and runbook addition.
